bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the title page ('LIMNOLOGY AND OCEANOGRAPHY 409 MAY 1976, V. 21(3)'; pp. 409–417)

claims.claim: nutrient-depleted cells sank about four times faster than growing ones (cited as abstract only)
claims.location: p. 410 (PDF p. 2), Results and Table 1; p. 409 (PDF p. 1), Abstract
claims.quote: the ratio of sinking rates of stationary phase to exponential phase cultures is 4.0
claims.conditions: laboratory batch cultures at 20 °C, 14:10 h light, WC medium; four species (Cyclotella meneghiniana, Scenedesmus quadricauda, Asterionella formosa, Melosira agassizii); 4.0 is the stationary/exponential ratio at the midrange size (10-µm radius) from a log–log regression; the species' own ratios are 3.0 (not significant), 3.3, 7.4 and 2.8 (Table 1); 'stationary phase' stands for nutrient-depleted cells
claims.note: The full text is now read, so '(abstract only)' can be dropped.

claims.source_value: the ~4× is stationary-phase versus exponential cultures grown in complete medium (WC, 50 µM phosphate; the limiting nutrient is not identified), all four species (ratio 4.0 at a 10-µm radius). For P-limited cultures, P enrichment cut the sinking rate to 16 % of its value within 7 days in Melosira (from 2.8 m/d) and to 50 % within 48 h in Scenedesmus
claims.location: p. 410 (PDF p. 2), Methods and Table 1; p. 411 (PDF p. 3), Fig. 1 text; p. 412 (PDF p. 4)
claims.quote: from exponential and stationary phase cultures grown in complete medium
claims.note: Say 'nutrient-depleted (stationary-phase) cells ~4× faster' rather than 'P-starved'; the P-limitation experiments give 2× (Scenedesmus, 48 h) to ~6× (Melosira, 7 days).

notes: Table 1 sinking rates (m/d, exponential → stationary): Cyclotella 0.08 → 0.24; Scenedesmus 0.27 → 0.89; Asterionella 0.20 → 1.48; Melosira 0.67 → 1.87 — so 'small greens 0.02–0.3' in config.js:1557 fits growing Scenedesmus but stationary Scenedesmus sank 0.89, and the diatoms span 0.08–1.87. The authors also argue that the usual loss = sinking rate / mixed depth may greatly overestimate losses in Langmuir circulation (abstract; Fig. 6). The measuring method covers about 0.1 to 20 m/d (p. 410). config.js:1553's 'Tilman & Kilham 1976 0.62' (a Monod Ks) names Tilman, not Titman: a different paper, not checked here; this one gives no Ks.
